parts.text: What is a probability generating function?
are the coefficients of each term.
A probability generating function is an encoding of a probability distribution
as a power series. For a finite set of outcomes, it is a polynomial.
The powers in a probability generating function are non-negative integers, corresponding to the possible outcomes.
It seems a bit bizarre to use write a probability distribution as a polynomial, when they seem to have no conceptual connection.
We will see that there are operations on probability distributions, e.g.
, where we can combine/manipulate their polynomial forms in a certain way.
: we can quickly multiply polynomials or differentiate them. Therefore,
it is often easiest to work on their polynomial form instead
, and where relevant, convert the resulting polynomial back into a standard probability distribution form. e.g.:
We will see that to add two independent random variables,
, we just multiply their probability generating functions:
will always be 1 for all random variables
, because substituting in 1 gives us the sum of the coefficients of the polynomial; these are the probabilities, and we know these sum to 1.
The last of these is the same as the probability generating function of
You’re implicitly using this one when you form a polynomial with the outcomes as the powers and the probabilities as the coefficients.
